Business insurance

Public Liability Insurance in Kenya

Public liability insurance responds when your business is legally liable for injury to a member of the public or damage to their property. A customer slips in your reception, a contractor’s tool damages a neighbour’s wall, a guest is hurt at an event you host. Without cover, you pay the claim and the legal costs yourself.

Request a quoteSpeak to an advisor

General information only. What is covered, the terms and the premium depend on the insurer’s policy wording, your circumstances and the information you disclose. Nothing here is a promise of cover.

What it covers

  • Legal liability for bodily injury to third parties
  • Legal liability for damage to third-party property
  • Legal costs and expenses, subject to the policy terms
  • Liability arising from your premises, and in many policies from your business activities away from premises

Who needs it

  • Shops, restaurants, hotels and event venues
  • Contractors and service providers working on client sites
  • Property owners and landlords of commercial buildings
  • Businesses asked for proof of liability cover in tenders or contracts

Common risks

Premises accidents

Wet floors, loose fittings, stairs and poor lighting are common sources of injury claims.

Work on other people’s property

Damage caused while performing work at a client’s site is a typical liability scenario for contractors.

Contract demands

Many contracts specify a minimum limit of indemnity. Check before you sign, not after.

Important considerations and exclusions

  • Public liability does not cover injury to your own employees. That is the role of WIBA and employer’s liability.
  • It does not cover professional errors in advice or design. That is professional indemnity.
  • Damage to property in your care, custody or control, and product liability, are often treated separately.
  • Policies set a limit of indemnity per event and may carry an excess.

What affects the premium

  • Business activity
  • Premises type and customer footfall
  • Limit of indemnity requested
  • Turnover or contract values
  • Claims history

Premiums are set by insurers, so we do not publish figures. Tell us about your situation and we will explain what is driving the quotation.

What we need for a quotation

  • Business activity and locations
  • Annual turnover
  • Limit of indemnity wanted or required by contract
  • Whether work is done on client premises
  • Existing policy and claims history

How Chestnut can help

We explain the cover in plain language, collect the information insurers need, approach suitable insurers for terms, and help with renewals and claims. Policies are issued by insurers, and you decide what to buy.

Frequently asked questions

What is the difference between public liability and professional indemnity?

Public liability deals with physical injury or damage to third parties. Professional indemnity deals with financial loss caused by errors in professional advice or services. Many professional firms need both.

How much cover should I buy?

The limit should reflect the worst plausible claim for your activities and any contractual minimum. We help you compare limits and the premium difference between them.
